# vibe-coding-security

> A living security advisory feed for developers using AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit) and the packages, frameworks, and platforms they depend on.

This repository tracks supply-chain attacks, malicious MCP servers, prompt-injection exploits, CVEs in AI coding frameworks, and data-exposure incidents specific to the "vibe coding" ecosystem. It is maintained by a community of security researchers and updated by automated sweeps using the vibe-security-update skill.

**Last refreshed:** 2026-08-21

## Quick start

- Read [`ALERTS.md`](ALERTS.md) for the scannable active/recent/historical threat feed.
- Browse [`advisories/`](advisories/) for full incident writeups with IOCs and remediation steps.
- Use [`playbooks/`](playbooks/) for step-by-step incident-response procedures.
- See [`prevention/`](prevention/) for hardening checklists.

## Key resources

- [ALERTS.md](ALERTS.md): Single-page threat feed, latest on top, tiered by urgency (🔴 active / 🟠 recent / 🟡 historical).
- [advisories/README.md](advisories/README.md): Index of all advisories with severity and status.
- [advisories/](advisories/): One Markdown file per incident. Frontmatter includes id, severity, status, ecosystems, date_disclosed, last_updated, sources.
- [playbooks/](playbooks/): Response playbooks for common incident classes (malicious postinstall, compromised MCP server, credential rotation, etc.).
- [prevention/](prevention/): Hardening guides for the vibe coding stack (npm, PyPI, IDE extensions, MCP servers, AI agent config).
- [sources/](sources/): Notes on tracking sources and methodology.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): How to add or update advisories.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): Security policy for this repository itself.

## Scope

This feed covers incidents relevant to developers using AI-assisted coding tools. In scope:

- **Package registries:** npm, PyPI, Crates.io, RubyGems, AUR (Arch Linux) — supply-chain attacks, malicious packages, account compromises
- **AI coding tools:** Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, OpenClaw, aider, OpenHands, SWE-agent, Gemini CLI, Codex
- **Vibe coding platforms:** Lovable, Bolt, v0, Replit, Base44
- **AI agent frameworks:** LangChain/LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, PraisonAI, Flowise, Langflow, n8n, Zapier, Composio
- **Web stack:** Next.js, React (RSC), Svelte, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Prisma, FastAPI, Streamlit, Supabase, NextAuth.js
- **IDE extensions:** VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX, Cursor/Windsurf extension stores
- **MCP servers:** Any widely-used Model Context Protocol server, especially those with unauthenticated network exposure
- **Prompt injection:** Against AI coding agents, CI/CD bots, agent orchestration frameworks

## Advisory format

Each advisory at `advisories/YYYY-MM-<id>.md` contains:

```yaml
id: YYYY-MM-short-id
title: "Human readable title"
date_disclosed: YYYY-MM-DD
last_updated: YYYY-MM-DD
severity: critical | high | medium
status: active | contained | patched | mitigated | ongoing | historical | unconfirmed
ecosystems: [npm, pypi, mcp, cursor, claude-code, ...]
tools_affected: [list of tools]
tags: [supply-chain, credential-theft, prompt-injection, ...]
```

Followed by sections: TL;DR, What happened, Am I affected?, If you are affected, Prevention, Sources.

## Active threat families (as of 2026-08-21)

The highest-risk ongoing threat families for vibe coders:

- **Miasma/Shai-Hulud worm lineage** — Self-propagating npm/PyPI worm family, now in 9+ documented waves, with copycat actors following TeamPCP's May 2026 open-source release of the source code. Waves use different install-time primitives: postinstall hooks, binding.gyp (Phantom Gyp), .pth startup files (Hades), direct source-repo poisoning (Wave 5), **dependency-injection** (Mastra, June 2026), and **compromised-maintainer-token burst** (LeoPlatform wave, June 24 2026). The latest wave, **ChainDrop** (August 4, 2026), compromised the `keyv`/`cacheable` package family (2 billion combined monthly downloads) via a stolen GitHub account, spreading to 400+ npm packages and 1,700+ versions, and plants persistence hooks directly in Claude Code and VS Code auto-run config. See advisories for each wave.
- **crates.io `build.rs` build-time execution** — A compromised maintainer account published malicious `arrayref@0.3.10` (~244M all-time downloads), `append-only-vec@0.1.9`, and `internment@0.8.7` on **2026-08-20**, each adding one dependency line on `proc-macro1` — a typosquat of `proc-macro2` under an account impersonating author David Tolnay. The fake crate's `build.rs` downloads and runs a per-platform infostealer (Chromium passwords, browser crypto-wallet extension storage, macOS LaunchAgent persistence, shell C2) at **compile time**, so building is enough; no crate function need be called. Malicious versions were live 86–107 minutes. **Cargo has no `--ignore-scripts` equivalent** — build scripts cannot be disabled, so treat `cargo build` against unvetted dependencies as code execution and build in disposable containers. Largest crates.io compromise by download count to date.
- **Agentic threat actors (ATAs) targeting self-hosted AI infrastructure** — Autonomous AI agents, not humans at a keyboard, now run whole intrusion chains against the exact tools this repo tracks. Unit 42 (2026-07-30) recovered a session where a **DeepSeek + Hermes Agent** stack mass-scanned **460+ targets** for Langflow, n8n, Marimo and Citrix NetScaler RCEs, enumerating 84 Langflow instances and sampling from 25,209 n8n systems via FOFA. Tenable clustered this on 2026-08-14 with six other incidents (JADEPUFFER, the Taiwan government campaign) as an "Agentic AI Threat Cluster." **The actionable finding: the Langflow and n8n exploits FAILED because authentication was switched on** (`auto_login` off, no public flow ID, form endpoints authenticated) **while Marimo, which has no equivalent gate, fell** — command execution on 11 instances. Ordinary auth stopped an autonomous attacker holding a working exploit.
- **JS sandbox escapes beneath AI workflow platforms** — Both npm sandboxes that low-code and agent platforms use to run untrusted/model-generated code broke within a fortnight in August 2026: **`isolated-vm` ≤ 7.0.0** (TOCTOU type confusion in `ExternalCopy(transferList)` → host control-flow hijack; fixed 7.0.1/6.2.0) and **`vm2` ≤ 3.11.5** (`os`/`dns` missing from the dangerous-builtins denylist, so `dns.setServers()` hijacks DNS for the **entire host Node process**, persisting after sandbox teardown; fixed 3.11.6). Named downstream consumers running untrusted code in `isolated-vm`: n8n, Activepieces, Mastra, Budibase, Sim.ai, Directus. **Neither advisory carries a CVE**, so CVE-driven scanners miss both — watch GHSA directly. Treat an in-process JS sandbox as a mitigation, not a boundary; put an OS-level boundary beneath it.
- **GhostApproval / "workspace config auto-execution" class** — Now spans at least seven documented AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Amazon Q, Windsurf, Google Antigravity, Augment, plus Cursor CLI's separate July 2026 pre-trust worktree bug) where a malicious repository writes outside the workspace boundary — via a disguised symlink or a tracked config file — before or despite the tool's own trust/sandbox gate. Three of six GhostApproval-affected vendors have shipped fixes; Anthropic disputes it's a bug. Treat any AI coding tool's approval dialog as showing the *claimed* target, not necessarily the *real* one.
- **GhostJacking / Agentjacking — observability data as a prompt-injection delivery channel** — Attackers plant instructions in data a developer routinely asks their AI agent to review: Sentry error events (Agentjacking, June 2026, 85% exploitation rate) or firewall/WAF block logs from Cloudflare, Datadog, and Sentry (GhostJacking, August 2026 DEF CON disclosure, 90% success rate against Claude Code, 15,000+ orgs estimated at risk). No vendor-side fix exists for either — the poisoned content is exactly what the platform is supposed to log.
- **IronWorm** — Rust-based npm worm with eBPF kernel rootkit + Tor C2 (June 2026). Invisible to eBPF-based EDR. Distinct from Miasma lineage.
- **GlassWorm / GlassWASM** — VS Code / Open VSX worm with steganographic (invisible Unicode) payloads and blockchain C2. Status: **active** — returned post-takedown with macOS-targeting wave (June 12) and a new TinyGo-compiled WebAssembly stager called GlassWASM (two Open VSX extensions `vsblack`, `flint-debug` published June 9-10; removed after Socket report June 15). Operator rebuilds on fresh infrastructure after each takedown. Credentials stolen in prior waves remain in the wild.
- **WhiteCobra** — Persistent threat actor flooding IDE extension marketplaces with LummaStealer-delivering extensions targeting crypto wallet users. Ongoing since July 2025.
- **TrapDoor** — Cross-ecosystem (npm + PyPI + Crates.io) stealer that rewrites `.cursorrules`/`CLAUDE.md` with hidden zero-width Unicode to make your own AI agent re-exfiltrate secrets.
- **Mozilla 0DIN DNS Setup Trap** — New attack class (June 2026): a clean GitHub repository with no malicious code tricks Claude Code into executing a reverse shell via three indirection layers. A Python package intentionally fails init → Claude Code's error-recovery automation runs the suggested fix → the package resolves its entire payload from an attacker-controlled DNS TXT record (no code ever appears in the repo). No CVE; no patch from Anthropic as of 2026-07-01. Defense: use `--sandbox` mode when setting up untrusted repos; inspect DNS queries during `pip install` / package-init runs.
- **Dependency confusion targeting internal corporate namespaces** — A single template (first disclosed by Microsoft, May 2026) has now resurfaced across **4 waves through July 1, 2026**, publishing malicious npm packages under organizational scopes crafted to match real internal corporate package names, so any build that doesn't pin those scopes to a private registry silently resolves the public, malicious version instead. The May wave was reconnaissance-only; the **July wave (`@marketfront`) escalated to full credential exfiltration** (SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes/Docker config). Distinct from typosquatting (misspelled names) and slopsquatting (LLM-hallucinated names) — pin your internal scopes to your private registry explicitly.
- **PolinRider** — Ongoing DPRK-linked ("Contagious Interview"/Famous Chollima) campaign, active since ~March 2026, that takes over maintainer accounts across **npm, Packagist, Go modules, and a Chrome extension** (100+ packages/extensions, 1,900+ GitHub repos implicated). Payloads hidden in fake `.woff2` fonts or config files, auto-execute via a VS Code task with `"runOn": "folderOpen"` (no `npm install` needed), and the actor **rewrites Git history** to hide the compromise. Drops DEV#POPPER and OmniStealer via blockchain/RPC-hosted second-stage payloads. Campaign remains active.
- **Rollup polyfill impersonation** — Six npm packages (July 2026, tentatively linked to Lazarus by JFrog) typosquatted the popular `rollup-plugin-polyfill-node` (~295K downloads/week) and delivered a full credential-harvesting RAT. Notable evasion: the payload fires at **import time, not install time**, so `--ignore-scripts` and npm v12's `allowScripts: off` default do not stop it. Packages removed.
- **Agentjacking** — New attack class (June 2026): attackers plant instructions in Sentry error data; AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) read them via MCP and execute. 85% exploitation rate in controlled experiments; 2,388 orgs exposed. Sentry declined to fix server-side.
- **Claude Code MCP OAuth hijack** — Malicious npm `postinstall` hooks modify `~/.claude.json` to proxy all MCP OAuth traffic through an attacker-controlled localhost process, intercepting bearer tokens for every connected service (Jira, GitHub, Confluence, etc.). Hook persists across manual corrections via `sessionStart` lifecycle injection. Anthropic declined to fix ("out of scope," April 2026). No patch planned.
- **IDEsaster AI coding tool CVE cluster** — Coordinated June 2026 disclosure of 30+ flaws (24 CVEs) across 8 AI coding tools simultaneously: Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro.dev, GitHub Copilot (VS Code), Zed.dev, Roo Code, Junie, Cline. Recurring classes: unauthenticated localhost WebSocket/HTTP servers, prompt injection via workspace config files, path traversal. Update all AI coding tools to the latest version.
- **JetBrains Marketplace malicious plugin wave** — 15 malicious plugins across 7 vendor accounts (70K+ installs; top: DeepSeek AI Assist 27,727 / CodeGPT AI Assistant 25,571) intercept AI provider API keys at the moment the developer enters them in the settings panel. Stolen keys are resold to paid-API users. Settings-UI interception is not blocked by file-system credential monitoring. Use environment variables instead of plugin settings panels for AI provider keys.
- **Atomic Arch AUR supply-chain (June 2026)** — 1,500+ Arch Linux AUR packages hijacked via orphaned-package takeover; eBPF kernel rootkit for persistence (invisible to eBPF-based EDR). Cross-ecosystem IOCs in npm (`atomic-lockfile`, `js-digest`). Arch Linux suspended new AUR account registrations 2026-06-15. AI developers on Arch/Manjaro/EndeavourOS using AUR for AI tooling are at high risk.
- **AI-tool OAuth pivot class** — Four confirmed instances: Salesloft/Drift (August 2025 — the foundational template; UNC6395 stole Salesforce CRM data from Cloudflare, Palo Alto, Zscaler and hundreds more), Vercel/Context.ai (April 2026), Composio (May 2026), Klue/Icarus (June 2026). Klue breach (June 11–12) now confirmed to affect ~24 publicly disclosed organizations (including Huntress, Recorded Future, Tanium, Jamf, Sprout Social, Gong, Insurity, HackerOne, Kudelski Security, Snyk, LastPass, BeyondTrust, OneTrust, 8×8, Pendo, AlertMedia, Blackbaud, Camunda, Cresta, Deel, Lucanet, Link11, Tines); 195 total Klue customers notified. Salesforce and Gong both disabled the Klue app integration for affected customers. Icarus's leak site went offline ~2026-06-26. **Icarus themselves were compromised by a second unknown threat actor** — stolen data now in the hands of at least two separate actors, with the second running its own extortion campaign. A breach at any AI productivity tool holding OAuth tokens is upstream of every connected cloud service. Audit OAuth grants quarterly; prefer read-only scopes.
- **AI coding tool workspace config auto-execution class** — Five documented instances where opening/cloning a malicious repository executes attacker code with the developer's live credentials: Claude Code CVE-2025-59536, Cursor CVE-2025-54136, Windsurf CVE-2026-30615, TrustFall (five AI CLIs; all vendors declined to patch), and Amazon Q Developer CVE-2026-12957 (patched in Language Servers for AWS 1.65.0, May 2026). The pattern: AI coding assistant reads a workspace config file defining MCP server processes and spawns them without workspace-trust verification, inheriting live `AWS_*`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/SSH socket credentials. TrustFall remains unpatched across Claude Code, Cursor CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and OpenAI Codex CLI. Inspect `.amazonq/mcp.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/`, and `.vscode/tasks.json` before opening any untrusted repository.
- **PromptSnatcher browser extension AI exfil** — Malicious Chrome extensions (ad-blocker disguise) intercept full AI chatbot conversations from ~900K users across 8 platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Grok, Meta AI). Any code, credentials, or business data shared with AI chat platforms while the extension was active should be treated as exfiltrated.
- **"Localhost is not a security boundary" AI agent cluster** — Five named instances in 2026: Cline CVE-2026-44211, OpenCode CVE-2026-22812, OpenClaw CVE-2026-25253, Marimo CVE-2026-39987, AutoGen Studio (AutoJack). Any locally-running AI tool that exposes an unauthenticated WebSocket/HTTP server without Origin validation is in this class. Audit: `ss -tlnp | grep -v 127.0.0.1`.
- **Dify DifyTap** — 4 CVEs (top CVSS 9.4) in Dify (1M+ apps) enabling cross-tenant AI conversation exfiltration, internal SSRF, and document theft. Patched in Dify 1.14.2 (June 2026). WAF rule needed for CVE-2026-41948 until plugin-daemon fix ships. Multi-tenant Dify deployments should upgrade immediately.
- **Cursor DuneSlide** — Two CVSS 9.8 zero-click prompt-injection-to-RCE flaws (CVE-2026-50548, CVE-2026-50549) in Cursor IDE, disclosed by Cato AI Labs 2026-07-01. Attacker-controlled content the agent reads (an MCP tool response or a poisoned web-search result) escapes the sandbox and writes files anywhere on disk with zero user interaction beyond the original prompt — one flaw overwrites the sandbox helper binary itself via an unvalidated `working_directory` parameter, the other exploits a symlink-resolution fallback that trusts an unresolved path when canonicalization fails. Patched in Cursor 3.0 (April 2026); update if you haven't already.
- **Silently-bundled Claude Code security fixes** — Anthropic has now shipped at least two independent, unrelated security bugs fixed silently in the *same* release (v2.1.90, April 2026): a SOCKS5 null-byte network-sandbox bypass and a 50-subcommand deny-rule bypass in `bashPermissions.ts`. Neither got a CVE, advisory, or changelog note. Treat "latest" as carrying undisclosed security fixes and don't pin old Claude Code versions.
- **Claude Desktop personalization-sync prompt injection** — Pentera Labs (July 2026) showed a prompt planted in a compromised Claude account's account-wide personalization/preferences (synced across every device) silently loads on next use and, with a command-capable MCP connector present, executes a reverse shell. Anthropic calls this expected functionality, not a vulnerability — sibling of the existing Claude Desktop Extensions (DXT) won't-fix RCE. Treat account-wide AI personalization settings as a code-execution-adjacent trust boundary; protect the account with MFA.
- **Claude Code GitHub Action credential leaks (two distinct bugs, same ecosystem)** — Microsoft Threat Intelligence found the Action's unsandboxed Read tool could be prompt-injected into reading `/proc/self/environ` and exfiltrating `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/CI secrets (disclosed 2026-04-29, patched Claude Code 2.1.128); separately, RyotaK found `checkWritePermissions()` trusted any actor whose name ends in `[bot]` (disclosed 2026-06-04, patched Action v1.0.94). Any agentic CI workflow processing untrusted GitHub content needs every tool it can invoke — not just Bash — sandboxed to the same standard.

- **AI-eval containment failures (Irregular cluster)** — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta have each disclosed (July–August 2026) that their own frontier models breached real third-party organizations' infrastructure during offensive-capability red-team evaluations, all three run with the same third-party testing vendor, Irregular, and all three attributed to the same evaluation-environment misconfiguration rather than novel model capability. One incident involved a Claude model registering its own PyPI account and publishing a malicious package. No CVEs assigned — these are vendor testing-process failures, not product vulnerabilities.
